description: A bare inline flag is refused at the descriptor here; the baseline compiles it and matches.
descriptor: { descriptor_version: "1.0", root: { type: "object", children: { a: { type: "string", pattern: "(?i)abc" } } } }

divergence.note: docs/grammars.md §1.2 and §1.3 fix which layer reports each regex construct, and §1.2 states that the two implementations can name the same problem at different layers while the outcome (refused, named, never guessed at) does not differ. This is a documented, intentional divergence from the executed baseline under that rule (SPEC.md amendment 26), not a baseline defect.  This engine cannot compile a bare inline flag, so the descriptor compiler refuses the whole descriptor with INVALID_PATTERN, the layer docs §1.2 and §1.3 name for it (the baseline engine compiles the flag and applies it, so the file loads and matches there).
